_README: Findings the owner has EXPLICITLY ACCEPTED. Read by scripts/check-publish-safety.mjs.
Entries name a RULE and a PATH GLOB — never a value. A file that spells out the
string it is allowing would be the leak it is meant to document.
Accepted is NOT hidden: the gate still prints a running count of accepted findings on
every run, so this list stays visible and can be revisited. Adding an entry needs an
owner decision and a reason, not a convenient silence.
To see everything including accepted:  npm run publish-safety:all -- --show-accepted

reason: The channel name is in 182 lines across 136 tracked files — the briefs, every
topics/*/long.json, channel_profile.md, docs/CONTINUE_HERE.md, and hardcoded in
scripts/build-linux-spec.mjs. It re-entered when the specs and briefs became
tracked (fa533ec), undoing part of what e746553 stripped.
Owner ruling: LEAVE IT. The channel is public on YouTube, so this is linkage
between the repo and a public brand, not exposure of a secret. Scrubbing forward
would leave it in history anyway, and a rewrite was judged disproportionate.
A future session must NOT 'helpfully' scrub this. It is a decision, not an
oversight. Reopen it only if the owner says so.
A personal handle is used as the sample home directory and shell prompt in the
Linux course content and in component fixtures — it is on screen in the shipped
video, so it is already public. Accepted under the same ruling as the channel name.
Scoped deliberately to course content and fixtures: a real home path appearing in
docs/, webui/ or anywhere else still BLOCKS, because that would be new disclosure
rather than this accepted one.
The Playwright Dojo specs demonstrate filling a login form, and the fixture address is
a Matrix joke. All ten flagged lines are the SAME invented address; every one was read
before this entry was written, and none is a real mailbox or the operator's.
Scoped to the pw-dojo topic specs on purpose. An email anywhere else — briefs/, docs/,
scripts/, another topic — still BLOCKS, because that would be a new disclosure rather
than this reviewed one.
These 96 specs lived only on the Windows laptop and were in no git history on any
machine; tracking them is what this entry unblocks.
Five findings, all the same string: an address in the support-email sample that the
Laya demo script triages on camera. It is INVENTED data, not a person's address —
the domain does not resolve and has no MX record (SERVFAIL on both), and the local
part belongs to a fictional customer in a fictional duplicate-charge complaint.
'Northwind' is the classic sample-database name, which is where the shape came from.
It is also already public: the string is baked into the filmed footage at s20 of the
shipped cut, which is on YouTube. Removing it from the repo would hide nothing.
Owner ruling, asked directly: accept — 'I dont want you to re record anything.' The
only alternative was re-recording the Laya take, since the address is in the frame.
Scope is deliberately narrow: this topic and its demo, not '**'. A NEW email in any
other file must still block. Do not widen this entry to make a future push pass.
